title: Algorithmic Fairness: Not a Purely Technical but Socio-Technical Property
reasoning: The paper critiques the purely mathematical framing of algorithmic fairness and argues for a socio-technical approach. While it discusses ethical concepts like equity and social justice to contextualize its arguments, it does not evaluate, benchmark, or study religion or specific moral/ethical systems themselves as a component of the research; it focuses on the properties of mathematical fairness metrics.
